approach: A rising air bubble in a denser viscous liquid reaches terminal velocity when the upward buoyant force is balanced by viscous drag, given by Stokes' law.

steps.text: Convert the given diameter to a radius.
Write the terminal velocity of a sphere rising through a denser viscous liquid.
steps.why_this_step: The bubble is far less dense than the liquid, so buoyancy pushes it up and viscous drag opposes the motion until the two balance.

steps.text: Substitute the given values and evaluate.

steps.equation: 0.53 mm/s is closest to the printed 0.5 mm/s

common_mistakes.text: Leaving out the factor of 2 in the formula and using r²(ρ_liquid − ρ_air)g/(9η) gives about 0.26 mm/s, which rounds toward 0.25 mm/s.
